units.title: Who is actually on Kittering Holm??? (just asking)
units.author: truthwatch_gil

edit.text: Who is on Kittering Holm? Just asking questions. Grieve won't give a number. Ardent Vale won't answer the Courier. The lights are on all night every night, which is not how a building site works, do your research. A private refuge for the rich needs somewhere with nothing around it, and that is exactly what a cleared island is. Somebody is being got ready for something.

units.text: Who is on Kittering Holm??? Just asking questions!!! Grieve won't give a number. Ardent Vale won't answer the Courier. The lights are on all night, every night!!! which is not how a building site works, do your research. A private refuge for the rich needs somewhere with nothing around it, and that is exactly what a cleared island is. Somebody is being got ready for something.

units.author: sb_mod
units.text: Thread title and opening post amended to remove excess punctuation, as per the board guidelines. Members are reminded that the people working on the Holm are private individuals doing their jobs. Discussion of the clearance is welcome. Speculation about the crew themselves is not. Sources, please, for any claim about the owner. Pell (Admin).

units.author: gilliver_lamp
units.text: I can see the camp lights from my front room. There are about eight of them, low down at the north end, and they comme on before I draw the curtains and are still on when I get up. I do not know who is there. I only know that it is a long way out and very cold, and that I keep my own lamp lit, as I always have.

units.author: skeptic_planner
units.text: Application ref ADC/VC/0917: 'total vegetation clearance, Kittering Holm, with associated temporary welfare facilities for contractors'. Temporary welfare facilities is the cabin and camper. Lights on all night at a remote camp are ordinary; you light a camp so people don't fall over. Clearing land before applying for anything else is a common and entirely legal way to raise its value.

units.author: fisher_bram
units.text: Aye, I see them from the creel line at five in the morning, Maud, still burning. Eight or nine. Steady. They keep a tidy camp from what I can see of it, which isn't much. Nobody's been on the Holm after dark since the curing men, and they never stopped long.

units.author: skeptic_brisk
units.text: It's a building site with the lights left on. My forecourt has the lights left on. Is my forecourt a refuge for the rich? Grow up.

units.author: hollow_signal
units.text: Some of us have known for a while what kind of place you build when you want nothing near you... and why you'd want it done in thirty days, before the long nights... I can't say more. Watch the lights. When they change, you'll know the work is finished... I've said too much already.

units.author: skeptic_ferrous
units.text: What would we expect to see if this were land speculation? A quick clearance, a quiet owner, no announcement until the permission is in. What would we expect if it were something sinister? Much the same, which is the problem with the theory: it predicts nothing. I'd ask what lights changing would prove, other than that someone switched a lamp off.

units.author: retired_teacher
units.text: May I gently say that 'who' takes a capital only at the start of a sentence, and that whoever is on that island is somebody's son or daughter, sister or brother. I taught a great many children who went on to do hard, cold jobs for decent pay. I should not like to think of them being discussed like this.

units.author: propwatch_ledger
units.text: Findings, week of the 19th: 1. No new filings by Ardent Vale Holdings this week. 2. The intermediary that bought the Holm has not changed its registered office. 3. Ardent Vale's annual accounts are due next month. 4. None of this proves anything either way. I'll keep checking. Apologies for the dull update; dull is what the registry is like.

units.author: truthwatch_gil
units.text: Accounts due next month. So right after the job finishes. Coincidence? Ledger has basically confirmed the timeline. Everything gets cleared, the accounts get filed, and then they move in. I've sent this to my list. Do your research people.

units.author: propwatch_ledger
units.text: Gil, I'm sorry, but I haven't confirmed anything of the kind. Annual accounts are due on a fixed date every year, based on when the company was formed. It would be due next month whether there was a Holm or not. Please don't send my findings to your list as if they say something they don't.

units.author: ex_grieve_corran

edit.text: I said I wouldn't post in these threads again. Just this. Some of us came back fine. From jobs like this one, I mean. Most of us. I'd like people to remember that before they make the crew into a story. I won't go into it.

units.text: I said I wouldn't post in these threads again. Just this. Some of us came back fine. From jobs like this one, I mean. Most of us. The ones who stuck to the camp rules did. I'd like people to remember that before they make the crew into a story. I won't go into it.

units.author: truthwatch_gil
units.text: Came back fine from what, exactly? 'Most of us'? What happened to the rest? You can't post something like that and walk away. What camp rules? This is exactly what I've been saying, there's something about these jobs nobody will talk about.

units.author: ex_grieve_corran
units.text: Nothing happened to the rest. Some went home early. People get homesick. Camp rules are camp rules, stay in after dark, don't wander off on your own, same as any site. I knew this would happen. That's me done.

units.author: sb_mod
units.text: A note to all members. A former worker has shared, briefly, that colleagues came home safely from a previous job, and has asked not to be questioned further. Please respect that. Repeated demands for personal information will be removed. Thank you to those who have kept this thread civil. Pell (Admin).

units.author: hist_wiki_marsh
units.text: Bram is right that overnight occupation of the Holm has been rare. The society has records of the 1890s timber camp, seasonal curing-station workers before the war, and a survey party in 1953 who did not stay after dusk. That's all we know of. Our wiki page on the window lamp custom has been updated this week, for anyone who asked.

units.author: skeptic_ferrous
units.text: Which tells us something useful: nobody has stayed overnight on the Holm because there has never been a reason to. No houses, no water supply, an awkward landing. The absence of people is about economics, not anything else. The first people with a reason to stay are the first people to stay. That seems to me the whole of it.

units.author: gilliver_lamp
units.text: I counted the camp lights again last night, because Bram asked me to on the telephone. I made it five, perhaps six. Fewer than before. I expect they have moved some lamps to where they are working. It is a big island. I have put a second lamp in my window, which is silly, I know.

units.author: truthwatch_gil
units.text: Fewer lights. So people are leaving. Or being moved. Ardent Vale won't answer. Grieve won't give numbers. Now the lights are going off one by one. I'm not saying anything I'm just putting the facts side by side.

units.author: skeptic_planner
units.text: Those are not facts side by side, Gil; they're a lamp count from across 9 km of water placed next to a guess. A clearance moves. As the trees come down the camp's working area shifts and lights get moved or turned off. If Maud's count halves again by the end of the month, that will mean the job is nearly done.

units.author: lh_insomniac_tollinby
units.text: I've been reading this thread at three in the morning, as one does. Maud, the second lamp isn't silly. There's an old novel where a woman leaves a light burning for a ship that has already come in, simply because she likes to think of the sailors seeing it. I always found that the kindest thing in the book.

units.title: Kids frightening each other about the island at school.
units.author: parent_tollinby
units.text: Is anyone else's primary schooler coming home with island stories? My middle one says a boy in her class told everyone the men on the Holm 'can't come back now', and she cried at bedtime. I've said it's a work camp and they come home when the job's done. Any tips? I don't want to make it a big thing. Also: does anyone know if the school's open if the power goes overnight?

units.author: skeptic_brisk
units.text: Tell her the men are on overtime and that's why they can't come back. Most frightening thing in the world, overtime. Seriously though, kids just repeat what they hear at home. Find out whose dad reads the TruthWatch list.

units.author: retired_teacher
units.text: In thirty-four years, the best answer I found was to give children a true, boring explanation and a job. Tell her the workers have a cabin, a kitchen and a boat that brings them porridge. Then ask her to draw the camp. Children who are drawing a kitchen are much less frightened than children who are imagining one. And the school will open; generators.

units.author: parent_tollinby
units.text: Mrs Hale, thank you, that worked. She drew a cabin with a very large porridge pot and a row of little beds and, for some reason, a dog. I didn't mention a dog, she just likes dogs. She's put it on the fridge. Also, new family moved in with the grandmother across our road yesterday, a little boy and a toddler, lovely kids. Mine have already taken him to see the swings.

units.author: sb_mod
units.text: A reminder that comments implying particular members' families are responsible for anything will be removed. CommonSenseCal, consider this a friendly first warning. The rest of this thread has been helpful and kind, which is rather what the board is for. Pell (Admin).

units.author: parent_tollinby
units.text: Update for anyone else dealing with this: the school sent a letter home asking parents to 'keep conversations about local news calm and factual'. Which is fair, but the boy who started it is the deputy head's nephew, apparently. Small towns. Anyway, mine slept fine last night. Thank you all.

units.author: skeptic_brisk
units.text: Fair enough, Pell. Withdrawn. For what it's worth I've got two of my own and they've started asking if they can sleep with the landing light on. Told them yes, because I'm not daft, it's 40 watts. Doesn't mean there's anything in it.

units.title: Power cuts. Freezers. Practical questions only, please.
units.author: parent_tollinby
units.text: Practical questions while the cuts keep happening: 1. How long is a full chest freezer actually safe if you don't open it? 2. Is it worth buying a little generator, or is that silly for a few hours a night? 3. Does anyone know if the co-op pays out for food? I lost a drawer of fish fingers in the Brackwater one and I'm still annoyed.

units.author: lineman_garvey
units.text: 1. Full chest freezer, lid shut, a day easy, longer in this cold. 2. Don't buy a generator for this, and if you do, never run it indoors or plug it into the house wiring. That's how linesmen get killed. 3. Only past twelve hours. Sorry about the fish fingers. We're doing what we can, it's flaming cold up there.

units.author: parent_tollinby
units.text: Thank you, that's really helpful, and no generator then. I didn't know about the plugging in thing. Stay warm up there. If you're ever doing the Tollinby line at school-run time, I'll bring you a tea, honestly.

units.author: skeptic_ferrous
units.text: On the cause, since people ask me: salt tracking on dirty insulators is very real. A season of fog lays down a film; it's harmless dry, conductive damp. Dew forms after midnight. A breaker trips. That fits the timing. It's dull, it's well understood and the fix is washing them, which is what they're doing. I'd be surprised if it were anything else.

units.author: wx_carrowpoint
units.text: For the record, my station saw thick salt fog on the night of the first cut: visibility 300 m at 23:00, relative humidity 98 per cent, a sticky film on the anemometer cups by morning. So Ferrous's mechanism had everything it needed that night. Tonight's forecast is the opposite: dry, calm, clear. We'll see.

units.author: sb_roadworks
units.text: Morning run update: temp lights at the Brackwater jct were dead at 05:40. Not red, not green, dark. Four of us sat there flashing headlights at each other like a courtship ritual until a tractor just went for it. Highways say they should be on battery. They were not on battery. They were on nothing.

units.author: lh_security_st
units.text: Same junction, same morning, about 05:20 on my drive home. Lights out. And yes, before anyone asks, the white van was there again, pulled onto the verge by the contractor's cabin, engine off, no one in the cab that I could see. I'll put the details in the van thread so this one stays practical.

units.author: sb_bins
units.text: Practical question. The council now says garden waste is suspended 'until the frost lifts' because frozen bins can't be emptied. My garden waste bin is not frozen. I have checked. It is full of leaves, dry leaves, under a lid. The newsletter on the 15th promised a full winter service. I quote it in full in my letter. Bernard (Rope Walk)

units.author: dc_3_wendell
units.text: Bernard, in Weyhaven they suspended ours in October and have not once mentioned it since. You are fortunate to have a newsletter to quote. I would also point out that the gulls are not suspended, and they do not wait for the frost to lift either.

units.author: sb_mod
units.text: Bernard, I'm moving the bins discussion to its own thread in General so this one stays about the power cuts, as the original poster asked. Your letter is, I'm sure, very thorough. Pell (Admin).

units.author: lineman_tess
units.text: CarrowPointWx, could I ask a favour? Could you send me your visibility and humidity for 22:00 to 03:00 on each night we've had a trip? I'm trying to line the trip times up against the weather properly rather than going by what it felt like on the pole. I'll share what I find, if I'm allowed.

units.author: wx_carrowpoint
units.text: Delighted to! I log every ten minutes and back it all up, as my wife will tell you at length. I'll pull the nights together tomorrow and post a table. Fair warning: the last two nights have been as dry as my station has seen all autumn, dew point well below the air temperature. Make of that what you will.

units.author: skeptic_ferrous
units.text: A fair test, and I'll look forward to the table. I'd note that frost forms on insulators even when the air is dry, by radiation on a clear night, and melts conductive at the first touch of current. So a dry night isn't automatically a clean one. But if the trips don't track moisture at all, I'll say so.

units.author: parent_tollinby
units.text: Update from my practical thread: Tollinby went off last night for two hours, freezer survived (lid shut, I sat on it, metaphorically), kids slept through, and I found out the warm space at the hall does soup. So, all fine. The linesman who answered me here: tea offer stands.

units.title: Update: not going to the Holm after all.
units.author: trades_holm_work
units.text: Quick update from Davey, for anyone who saw my posts in Trades. Never heard back from Grieve about subbing on the Holm, so I've took a hedge-cutting and flail job for two farms out past TOLLINby, three weeks, cash, home every night. Still got all tickets: CS30, CS31, CS38, telehandler. Still no job too small. Cheers all.

units.author: fisher_bram
units.text: Good lad. Home every night is worth more than the Holm rate, whatever they're paying. Hedges don't argue back.

units.author: ex_grieve_corran
units.text: Good. I meant what I said before. Take the hedges. Nothing against the lads out there. It's just better at home.

units.author: trades_holm_work
units.text: Cheers both. Wife's pleased, she never liked the sound of a month on an island anyway, said I'd go mad without the telly. She's probably right. If anyone needs a flail mower after Christmas, you know where I am.

units.author: sb_mod
units.text: This thread has been moved to Trades & Jobs, where it belongs. Members are reminded that self-promotion is welcome in Trades & Jobs and nowhere else. Best of luck with the hedges. Pell (Admin).

units.title: White van at the Brackwater junction.
units.author: lh_security_st
units.text: Posting before I sleep. Some of you know about the van that idled at the edge of our car park lights for four hours at the start of the month. White panel van, no livery, dent in the rear nearside door. This morning at 05:25 it was parked on the verge at the Brackwater junction by the temp lights. Engine running, cab dark. I didn't stop. Control says I'm obsessed.

units.author: sb_roadworks
units.text: Dent in the back door, nearside? Mate, I've passed that van at the jct twice this week on the 05:45 run. Parked tight to the contractor's cabin. Thought it was the contractor's. It isn't, their vans are yellow and they don't start till eight. Didn't see anyone in it either time.

units.author: skeptic_ferrous
units.text: There must be a few hundred white panel vans in the Sound with a dent in them. What would we expect if it were the same van? Matching plates, ideally. Did either of you get the registration? Without it this is two sightings of a common object at a junction lots of vans use.

units.author: lh_security_st
units.text: Fair, and I didn't get the full plate, it was too dirty. I've got the last three letters from the car park footage at the start of the month, though, from Control's camera. Next time I see it at the junction I'll get the rest. If it matches, I'll post. If it doesn't, I'll post that too.

units.author: sb_mod
units.text: Moved to Local Oddities. A reminder that registration numbers must not be posted in full on this board, even if obtained. Please send them to the police if you believe a vehicle is involved in an offence. An idling van is not, as far as I know, an offence. Pell (Admin).

units.author: lh_security_st
units.text: As promised. Junction, 05:20 today, lights out because of the cut. Van on the verge again, engine off this time, frost all over the windscreen so it had been there a while. Last three of the plate match the car park footage. I didn't get out. I'm not posting the plate, Pell. Make of it what you like.

units.author: sb_roadworks
units.text: Gone this morning. Verge has a dry patch the shape of a van where the frost didn't settle, so it was there most of the night. Highways had their generator on the temp lights so at least we had red. Somebody's sleeping in it, bet you. Poor sod, minus five.

units.title: Carrow Point station: daily readings (19th).
units.author: wx_carrowpoint
units.text: Day 19 summary: max 5.2C, min 0.4C. Pressure 1031 hPa and rising steadily, a lovely clean climb. Wind NW 18 km/h this morning dropping to 4 by sunset. Visibility 40 km plus this afternoon; I could count the lamp posts on Lisle pier. Dew point falling fast. The high is arriving exactly as the Met Office drew it, for once. Frost tonight.

units.author: wx_carrowpoint
units.text: Day 20 morning: min minus 3.1C at the station, minus 4.8C on the grass. Pressure 1038 hPa. Wind: calm since 01:30, the anemometer has not turned once. I noticed this before I looked at the logger, actually: my weather vane usually ticks against the bracket all night, and it was silent. Odd thing to miss. Calm cold spell has begun.

units.author: sb_commuter_lisle
units.text: Lovely, so the ferries have no fog to blame this week and still don't run at night. Thank you for the readings, honestly, they're the most reliable thing about my commute. Lisle pier was frozen solid this morning; the crew were out with buckets of grit at 07:00.

units.author: wx_carrowpoint
units.text: Day 21 morning: min minus 4.6C, a new low for the season here. Pressure 1040 hPa. Calm all night again, second night running with no measurable wind. Humidity 61 per cent at midnight, very dry for the coast. Sound carries absurdly: I could hear a dog in Gilliver at 02:00, and Gilliver is 7 km off. Not one gust to cover it.

units.author: fisher_bram
units.text: Aye, sound carries in this. On the creel line this morning I could hear the kettle whistle in Rook's back shop. Flat calm, not a ripple, the boats looked like they were sat on glass. Grand for fishing. Hard on the hands.

units.author: wx_carrowpoint
units.text: A kettle at that distance is about right in an inversion like this one: warm air sitting on cold water bends sound back down towards the surface. It's the same effect that lets you hear trains on a winter night. Lovely physics. I'll be up at three again tonight, I suspect, listening to the Sound.

units.title: Night ferries: still cut, still no explanation.
units.author: sb_commuter_lisle
units.text: Day five of the 'crew welfare review'. My sister works lates at Port Ammet General and now sleeps on a camp bed in the nurses' office twice a week because the 22:10 doesn't run. Nobody at Sound Lines will say what the review is about. If the crew are short-staffed, say so. If something happened, say so. I've started a petition.

units.author: retired_teacher
units.text: Ewan, I've signed your petition, and I've written to the community council as well. I would only add that the crews are Lisle and Gilliver people, several of whom I taught, and if they need time, they ought to have it. We managed with fewer boats once. It was not pleasant, but we managed.

units.author: ferry_skipper_odell
units.text: Speaking for myself and not the company. The review is real, it's about the crew, and it's being done properly. Nobody on the night boats is short-staffed by choice. New deck and slipway lighting has been ordered and we expect to be back on nights soon after it's fitted. I understand the frustration. Logged it, carrying on.

units.author: sb_commuter_lisle
units.text: Thanks, skipper, genuinely. That's more than the company's said in five days. But 'lighting has been ordered' makes me wonder what the lights are for. Ferries have run in the dark for a hundred years. What's changed that needs floodlights on the slipways?

units.author: skeptic_ferrous
units.text: I'd guess, from long experience of these reviews, that the crew have asked for better lighting at the slipways because of the trespass business earlier in the month, and the company has agreed. That is a perfectly ordinary outcome. Better light means fewer arguments about what someone saw in fog.

units.author: harbourmaster_quill
units.text: I'm sorry, but I can't comment on Sound Lines' internal review. What I can say is that the Gilliver slipway is a working slipway and that byelaw 14 prohibits anyone except authorised users from the lower section at any time. That has not changed. Improved lighting is welcome. Thank you.

units.author: lisle_crew_ada
units.text: I work the Lisle pier and I can tell you the crews aren't lazy, ha, they're... well. They're tired. It's been a funny few weeks. The new lights will help, I think. I signed your petition too, Ewan, because I'd like the late boat back as much as anyone. Ha. Anyway.

units.author: sb_commuter_lisle
units.text: Small win: from tomorrow there's a late water-taxi for hospital staff at 23:15, so my sister can come home. Still nothing for the rest of us, and still no word on what the review is actually about. 412 signatures. I'm taking it to the transport committee next month whether the boats are back or not.

units.author: retired_teacher
units.text: Well done, Ewan. 412 is a respectable number for an island our size. Do please check the petition wording before it goes to committee: 'stranded on the wrong side of the water' is vivid, but 'the' wrong side implies there is a right one, and the people of Port Ammet may take that personally.

units.title: Gritting: Gilliver hill missed.
units.author: sb_roadworks
units.text: 05:35. Port Ammet bypass gritted, lovely. Tollinby road gritted. Gilliver hill: not gritted, sheet ice from the chapel to the harbour, I watched a milk float do a slow pirouette. Brackwater jct temp lights dead again. If you're going down to Gilliver this morning, go in second and pray.

units.author: sb_bins
units.text: The council's gritting plan, published in the newsletter on the 15th, lists the Gilliver hill as a priority route. Page two, third item. I shall be pointing this out to them, along with the matter of the recycling crate they returned to my neighbour's drive instead of mine. Bernard (Rope Walk)

units.author: harbourmaster_quill
units.text: Thank you for the warning. The council gritter reached the Gilliver hill at 07:40 this morning; it had been held up behind a lorry on the bypass. The harbour road and the slipway approach have been salted by harbour staff. Please take care on the lower slipway, which ices at low water whatever we do.

units.author: sb_roadworks
units.text: Appreciated, harbourmaster. 07:40 is about two hours after every van in the Sound has already gone down that hill on its roof, but appreciated. Milk float driver was fine by the way, I stopped. He said it was the most exciting thing that's happened on his round since the cow.

units.author: sb_roadworks
units.text: 05:40 today: Gilliver hill gritted at last, the gritter must have gone out at four. Brackwater jct lights working on the generator, a little red light in the middle of nowhere, very festive. Minus five on the dash. Tollinby road has a frozen puddle the size of a swimming pool at the dip by the farm shop. You've been warned.

units.title: LowBand banned me lol (and what's coming next)
units.author: nightscream_vlog
units.text: guys so LowBand gave me a 'temporary suspension' for 'reuploading members' files without permission' which is insane because I credited them in the description, link in bio. whatever. their loss. big things coming, I'm planning a proper live investigation in Brackwater woods with thermal and everything. date TBC. you're not ready.

units.author: skeptic_brisk
units.text: You put spooky music over a man's owl recording and called it 'screaming in the woods (real)'. The owl has a better case for suing you than you have for complaining.

units.author: nightscream_vlog
units.text: cal mate nobody asked you. the owl thing was a thumbnail. the actual video had like four minutes of analysis in it. anyway at least I'm going out there, what are you doing, selling Corollas. stream date coming soon guys stay tuned

units.author: sb_mod
units.text: Two things. First, The Sound Board does not host promotion for streams or videos outside Trades & Jobs. Second, the Brackwater estate has asked members not to enter the woods at night, and this board will not be used to organise anyone doing so. This thread is now closed. Pell (Admin).

units.title: Where can you still get lamp oil?
units.author: parent_tollinby
units.text: Silly question maybe. Sound FM says the Gilliver chandlery has sold out. The hardware shop in Tollinby only has the scented stuff for garden torches, which I'm told you must not burn indoors. My mum has an old hurricane lamp she swears by and wants oil for it before the next cut. Anywhere else? Not looking to start a debate, just oil.

units.author: gilliver_lamp
units.text: Rook at the chandlery has more coming next week. In the meantime, I have three bottles in my scullery, which is more than an old woman needs. If your mother can get someone to Gilliver, she may have one, and welcome. Tell her to trim the wick short or it smokes. I have been doing it for seventy years and I still get it wrong.

units.author: parent_tollinby
units.text: Maud, that is so kind, thank you. Mum says she'll come over on the Saturday bus and bring you a cake, and will not be argued with. She says the wick thing is the bit everyone gets wrong. I'll stop asking silly questions now.

units.author: skeptic_brisk
units.text: Or buy a battery lantern for a tenner like a normal person in this century. Our forecourt shop has them by the till. I'm not even on commission. Paraffin lamps in a house with kids, honestly.

units.author: hist_wiki_marsh
units.text: For anyone interested, the society's holdings include a 1930s price list from the old Gilliver general store showing lamp oil as one of its top-selling lines, ahead of tea. Which says something about the village, though I'm not entirely sure what. Cal's point about safety is a good one, for what it's worth.

units.title: Found: child's red mitten, Port Ammet library.
units.author: lh_insomniac_tollinby
units.text: Found in the warm space at Port Ammet library this afternoon, under the newspaper rack: one small red knitted mitten with a white star on the back and a string to go through the sleeve. Very well loved. I've handed it to the desk. Posting in case the owner's parent reads this board at three in the morning, as I do.

units.author: sb_lostcat
units.text: Not mine, but thank you for posting it, people forget how much a lost thing matters to a small child. When Pebble (grey, one white sock, home safe now) went missing, someone posting a photo of a grey cat on a wall got me through a whole evening. I'll mention the mitten to the mums who come in the shop.

units.author: parent_tollinby
units.text: It might be my friend's daughter's, she was at the warm space yesterday with her nan. I'll send her the description. If it's hers she'll be thrilled, the other one has been sleeping on her pillow all night like a pet.
